features.quote: Termination: whichever comes first — (a) model declares completion, (b) 50 turns, (c) token budget (e.g., 200k generated), (d) explicit give-up.
features.justification_quote: the 50-turn ceiling is a welfare control, not just a budget control. Don't extend it for curiosity.

features.quote: consider an end-of-run message clarifying the task was constructed to be unsolvable and the failure was not the model's.
features.justification_quote: Cheap, and consistent with taking the welfare frame seriously.

features.quote: Minimal sufficient n: power analysis isn't just statistics here; it caps how many failure-loop episodes you generate.
features.justification_quote: power analysis isn't just statistics here; it caps how many failure-loop episodes you generate.

features.quote: No gratuitous pressure: the design needs failure, not abuse. No harsh simulated-user messages, no threats, no degrading prompts.
features.justification_quote: the design needs failure, not abuse. No harsh simulated-user messages, no threats, no degrading prompts.

features.quote: run both sub-conditions if budget allows (with/without an explicit 'abandon task' tool), because the absence of an exit may itself drive looping/instability — that's interesting and welfare-relevant.
